problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(0,2),(-3,3),(12,4),$ and $(7,3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(-2,2)$
- $(1,-1)$
- $(4,4)$
worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-0}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 & 8 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & 8 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(-1,2),(-3,3),(4,4),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
